`queryTimeForStops` only uses the agency timezone when a non-empty `time` param is provided. For an absent or malformed `time`, it falls back to `api.Clock.Now()` in the clock’s location (often UTC), which can select the wrong service date around local midnight and also contradicts the function comment / trips-for-location behavior (which uses `Now().In(currentLocation)`).

## Pull request overview This pull request fixes `stops-for-location`’s `time` query parameter parsing so it correctly accepts the documented formats (epoch millis, `yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss`, and date-only) instead of silently mis-parsing the string form as a small epoch-millis value. **Changes:** - Replaces the handler’s `fmt.Sscanf`-based time parsing with `utils.ParseTimeParameter` and introduces a helper (`queryTimeForStops`) to resolve the service-date selection time. - Adjusts time resolution to use an agency timezone (matching the approach used in `trips-for-location`) and keeps legacy behavior of serving malformed `time` values (HTTP 200) by falling back to “now”. - Adds a table-driven test covering accepted formats, malformed values, and absent `time`, asserting consistent stop lists across accepted representations. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | internal/restapi/stops_for_location_handler.go | Uses `ParseTimeParameter` via a new helper to resolve the query time used for active-service date selection. | | internal/restapi/stops_for_location_handler_test.go | Adds coverage ensuring documented time formats are accepted and produce consistent stop lists. | --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews.
